title: 信号処理
subtitle: Signal Processing
educationalGoal: (1) Learn the foundations of signal processing, including analog-to-digital conversion. (2) Understand the basic concepts for digital signals processing, including convolution, Z-transform, sampling theorem, and Fourier analysis. (3) Acquire the ability to evaluate signals transmitted between linear time-invariant (LTI) systems and to extract the features underlying signals.
advice: This is a basic course in signal processing for discrete time signals. We will mainly cover the following topics: 1. Basic concepts of digital signal processing. 2. Expressing LTI systems with linear convolution. 3. Expressing discrete time transfer functions using Z-transform and its frequency domain property. 4. Expressing Fourier series and Fourier transform for continuous and discrete time signals in relation to the sampling theorem. Students are expected to actively participate in class. Students are expected to complete exercises independently. Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.
books: Hitoshi Kiya, Digital Signal Processing (in Japanese), Ohmsha
requiredKnowledge: Sufficient mathematical calculation skills (especially those covered in Control Engineering I). Basic knowledge of differential and integral calculus.

activityGoals.body: Explain expressions of discrete time signals obtained by sampling various continuous time signals
Express the linear convolution of discrete time signals, Fourier series, and Fourier transform
Express the characteristics of transient responses and frequency responses of discrete LTI systems
